{{Short description|Uruguayan scientist}}
'''Lucrecia Covelo de Zolessi''' (12 January 1920 – 9 March 2000<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lucrecia Covelo de Zolessi {{!}} Autores.uy |url=https://autores.uy/autor/9765 |access-date=2022-07-09 |website=autores.uy |archive-date=2020-08-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200804080731/https://autores.uy/autor/9765 |url-status=dead }}</ref>) was a [[Uruguay|Uruguayan]] [[Entomology|entomologist]], curator and film-maker, who taught at the Faculty of Humanities and Sciences at the [[University of the Republic (Uruguay)|University of the Republic]], where she was Chair of the Entomology department.

== Biography ==
Covelo was part of the first cohort to study for a BA in Biological Sciences at the [[Faculty of Humanities and Sciences of Montevideo]] ([[:es:Facultad de Humanidades y Ciencias de la Educación (Universidad de la República)|es]]), a course which began in 1947. During her degree, she focussed the morphology and ethology of [[hymenoptera]] and [[Crustacean|crustaceans]].''<ref name=":0">Mones, Álvaro (August 2004). [https://www.mnhn.gub.uy/innovaportal/file/3684/1/zolessi_biobiblio.pdf "Bio-bibliography of Lucrecia Covelo de Zolessi"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220704170201/https://www.mnhn.gub.uy/innovaportal/file/3684/1/Zolessi_biobiblio.pdf |date=2022-07-04 }}. ''National Museum of Natural History and Anthropology''. Retrieved 9 July 2022.</ref>'' She was an early exponent of using film in the natural sciences, directing a film in 1959 on the sexual behaviours of ''[[Bothriurus|Bothriurus bonariensis]].<ref name=":0" />''<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YV1YAAAAMAAJ&q=Lucrecia+Covelo |title=IV Festival Internacional de Cine Documental y Experimental: Julio-Agosto de 1960 |date=1960 |publisher=SODRE |language=es}}</ref> From 1962 to 1963, she studied at the University of Sorbonne, and obtained her doctorate there. Her thesis examined the anatomy of lobsters.<ref name=":0" /> From 1967 she was a member of Sociedad Malacologica del Uruguay.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lucrecia Covelo de Zolessi {{!}} Shellers From the Past and Present |url=https://www.conchology.be/?t=9001&id=59233 |access-date=2022-07-09 |website=www.conchology.be |language=en |archive-date=2023-11-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231122140757/https://www.conchology.be/?t=9001&id=59233 |url-status=live }}</ref> 

As an entomologist, Covelo specialised in ants, and advised companies on pesticide control. She became a pioneer of the use of artificial anthills in South America,''<ref name=":0" />'' and more generally was a leading figure in the field.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Varini |first=Felipe S. Vázquez |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gb8eAQAAIAAJ&q=Lucrecia+Covelo+de+Zolessi |title=Las ciencias de aquí: crónicas |date=1994 |publisher=Crónicas |language=en}}</ref> One of her discoveries related to the oviposition in the ''[[Paulinia]]'' genus.<ref>Liebermann, José. [https://www.biotaxa.org/RSEA/article/view/48672/42133 "Sistematica de la oviposición epidafica en acridoideos (Orth. Caelif. Acrid.)."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210424063857/https://www.biotaxa.org/RSEA/article/view/48672/42133 |date=2021-04-24 }} ''Revista de la Sociedad Entomológica Argentina'' 20.3-4 (1957).</ref> She also worked on the feeding behaviour of ''[[Cornops aquaticum]]''.<ref>Carbonell, C. S. [https://repository.si.edu/bitstream/handle/10088/23775/1959%20vol%20137%20%20%20%20Smithsonian%20invertebrates%201-416.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y#page=72 "THE EXTERNAL ANATOMY OF THE SOUTH AMERICAN SEMIAQUATIC GRASSHOPPER MARELLIA REMIPES UVAROV (ACRID."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220709115340/https://repository.si.edu/bitstream/handle/10088/23775/1959%20vol%20137%20%20%20%20Smithsonian%20invertebrates%201-416.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y#page=72 |date=2022-07-09 }} ''Studies in Invertebrate Morphology'' (1959): 61.</ref>

From early in her career, Covelo was linked to the [[National Museum of Natural History, Uruguay|National Museum of Natural History]] (MNHN), first as a student and subsequently as a researcher and conservation lead on the Entomological Collection. She taught at the Faculty of Humanities and Sciences of Montevideo, where she was in charge of the [[Arthropod]] Department and the Entomology Chair.''<ref name=":0" />''
